source: ME5412 2. Mobility aids.pdf, smart-wheelchair sensor slides/pages 37-38, corroborated by indexed visual supplements
note: Evaluation-only extensions of Q25. These do not alter canonical V25 or product runtime.

variants.question: A smart wheelchair needs a sensor that scans the environment over a wide horizontal angle to support obstacle avoidance. Which named course sensor best matches this role?
variants.evidence: Laser range finder provides a 180-degree scan; force sensors are discussed in rehabilitation-robot sensing, not as the named smart-wheelchair example.

variants.question: Which smart-wheelchair sensor captures both an image and depth information for environmental perception?
variants.evidence: The slide describes stereovision camera as capturing image and depth.

variants.question: Microsoft Kinect is used in the course as an example of which sensing approach for a smart wheelchair?
variants.evidence: The slide names structured light, such as Microsoft Kinect.

variants.question: A wheelchair bumper makes contact with an obstacle and reports that contact. Which course term describes this sensor, and what must it not be confused with?
options: A. BUMP tactile sensor; it is not the same as a force sensor
B. Force sensor; it is identical to every force sensor
C. GPS; it is a position sensor
D. IMU; it measures acceleration and gyroscope data
variants.evidence: The slide names BUMP tactile sensing. The course supplement distinguishes contact/bump sensing from force sensors used in rehabilitation-robot sensor fusion.

variants.question: Which sensor estimates wheel rotation or traveled distance on the smart wheelchair itself?
variants.evidence: Wheelchair encoders are explicitly named in the smart-wheelchair sensor slide.

variants.question: Which named sensor is most directly associated with global positioning rather than local obstacle contact?
variants.evidence: GPS is explicitly named as a smart-wheelchair sensor and supplies global positioning; BUMP is contact sensing.

variants.question: Select all sensor examples explicitly named on the smart-wheelchair sensor slides. (Multiple answers.)
options: D. Structured light such as Kinect
variants.evidence: The slide list includes ultrasonic/sonar, infrared, laser range finder, stereovision, structured light/Kinect, BUMP tactile, encoders, IMU and GPS. Force sensor is not the BUMP/tactile category and is not selected in this smart-wheelchair list.
